sentences.text: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TUSHAR RAO GEDELA  OR % 18.09.2023
[The proceeding has been conducted through Hybrid mode]
1. Exemption allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

3. This is a bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C., 1973 seeking grant of anticipatory bail in FIR No. 146/2023 daed 16.05.2023 under Sections 420/406/120-B IPC, 1860 registered at Police Station Pul Prahladpur, Delhi.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/09/2023 at 21:21:44 4.
The applicant is the brother-in-law of the complainant.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submits that according to the version of the complainant, the disputes arose between the complainant and the family members of the late husband of the complainant, only after the death of late husband.

Sumit vs State & Anr on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196845342/
1

6. Learned counsel submits that there are multiple allegations against the applicant and the family members with respect to illegal sale of few properties, JCB machine as also Swift car, which is alleged to have been illegally sold by the applicant and the family members without obtaining the consent of the complainant.
7. Learned counsel submits that in view of the fact that these are family issues, though the mediation was sought, however the same failed in the past.
Learned counsel also submits that at the time of initial mediation, the applicant and the family members were ready to offer Rs.25 Lacs qua the FIR in question.
8. Issue notice.

9. Notice accepted by Mr. Mukesh Kumar, learned APP for State, who seeks and is granted four weeks' time to file the status report.
10.
Notice is also accepted by Mr. Deepkaran Dalal, learned counsel for the complainant, who is also present in person.

11. In view of the aforesaid submissions, this Court has interacted with the parties who are present in person and it appears that since the disputes are between erstwhile family members, the same can be still resolved even as on date.
12. The complainant has admitted that she is in possession of the JCB machine.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/09/2023 at 21:21:44 13.

In respect of the so called illegal sale and the sale considerations received by the applicant and his family members, learned counsel for the applicant submits, on instructions, that the applicant and his family is willing to deposit a sum of Rs.30 Lacs before this Court.
However, he requests that the same be directed to be paid in instalments.
The complainant has no objection in case such deposit is made.
14. Accordingly, no coercive steps shall be taken against the applicant by respondent no.1, subject to the investigations being continued.

Subject also to deposit of Rs.30 Lacs by the petitioner in the following manner:-
(a) A sum of Rs.15 Lacs shall be positively deposited within 15 days from today.
(b) A sum of Rs. 10 Lacs will be deposited within four weeks after the initial expiry of two weeks.

Sumit vs State & Anr on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196845342/
2
(c) The balance remaining Rs.5 Lacs shall be deposited within four weeks from the payment made in clause (b) above.
15. The aforesaid amount shall be deposited by the applicant strictly in accordance with the above schedule in the name of Registrar General of this Court.
16. The parties have shown interest to be referred to Mediation.
17. Accordingly, the parties are directed to appear before Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre on 22.09.2023 at 4:00 PM.
